description.database: Copies of this database, made on a schedule or by hand. Each one is an export of a single database, checked before it can be restored. Backup files are not encrypted by the panel: use a destination you trust.
description.volume: Copies of this service's named volumes. Files are read while the application runs, so a copy taken at a busy moment may not be consistent: stop the application first if it has to be exact. Backup files are not encrypted by the panel.

actions.noVolumes: This service has no named volume.
actions.destinationNotReady: Its destination can't be reached right now.

history.title: History
history.noneForFilter: Nothing here is in that state.

config.enabledHint: Off means it only runs by hand. If the panel was down at a scheduled time, it runs once when it comes back, never once per missed time.
config.cronHint: Minute, hour, day, month, weekday. Runs in the server's time zone.
config.providerLocalHint: This destination is on this server, so a copy here is lost with the server.
config.pathHint: Inside the destination. Letters, digits, dashes, dots and slashes.
config.retentionHint: How many scheduled runs to keep. Manual backups and safety copies are never counted.
config.deleteDescription: No more backups of this kind will be taken. Files already stored stay where they are.

scopeHint.database: One database and nothing else. Accounts are not part of it.
scopeHint.instance: Every database on this server, with its users and roles.
scopeHint.accounts: Users and roles only, with no data.

config.scheduleHint: When it runs, in the server's time zone.
config.providerHint: Where the backup file is kept.

run.title: Run this backup now
run.description: {{target}} is copied to its destination right away.
run.name: Name
run.nameHint: Shown in the history next to this run.

description.database: Tables and data in {{target}} that are also in the backup are replaced. The current data stays in place until the backup has been verified and a safety copy is taken first.
description.volume: The contents of {{target}} are replaced. The service stops briefly for the swap, and the old contents are kept in a folder next to the volume.
description.instance: Every database on {{target}} is replaced by what this file holds, including its users and roles. The backup is imported into a new, separate server and the service only moves over once that has worked. The current data is kept on its own volume, listed under Monitor, Storage.
description.accounts: The users and roles of {{target}} that are in this file are put back as they were. Data is not touched, the panel's own account stays as it is, and any account added since stays too.

fromPath.title: Restore from a file

description.database: For a backup this panel has no record of. A manifest must sit next to the file, and it is checked before anything changes.
description.volume: For a backup this panel has no record of. A manifest must sit next to the file, and it is checked before anything changes.

fromPath.pathHint: The full path inside the destination, ending in the file's name.
fromPath.scopeHint: It has to match the manifest next to the file.

restore.confirmHint: Typing the exact name confirms this is the right one.
restore.targetHint: What the backup replaces. Its current content is overwritten.

errors.schedule: Enter a valid cron expression, or pick a preset
errors.retention: Enter a whole number, or leave it empty
errors.path: Use letters, digits, dashes, dots and slashes
errors.restorePath: Enter the path of a file

description.database: Add one to copy this database to a destination you choose, on a schedule or by hand.
description.volume: Add one to copy a named volume to a destination you choose, on a schedule or by hand.

unresolved.title: A restore needs attention
unresolved.description: The panel could not tell how the last restore ended, so backups and restores on this service are held back until someone has checked it.
unresolved.resolveTitle: Is the data as you expect?
unresolved.resolveDescription: Only continue once you have looked at the database or volume yourself. This lifts the hold on backups and restores for this service.

deleteBackup.title: Delete this stored file?
deleteBackup.description: {{file}} is removed from its destination for good. Its line stays in the history.

discard.title: Delete the earlier copy?
discard.description: {{folder}} held the volume's contents before the restore. This removes it for good.
